source.title: STEM: Efficient Relative Capability Evaluation of LLMs through Structured Transition Samples
source.authors: Hai Hu; Jia-Zhi Jiang; Shi-You Xu; Ruhan Zeng; Tian Wang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes benchmark accuracy across model sizes and argues that benchmark difficulty can produce S-shaped performance curves and systematic departures from a linear fit. This refines or qualifies scaling-trend claims, but it does not test held-out cross-entropy scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The study's own Qwen3 benchmark scores and its analyses of their fit against log parameter count bear on downstream performance trends and curve shape. Table 1 reports results from official technical reports and is cited background, not a result counted here. The study does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, training tokens, training compute, or a compute-optimal parameter/token split.
record.test_reason: The study's own zero-shot, non-CoT accuracies for eight Qwen3 sizes (0.6B–235B) on six benchmarks (Table 8), and its linear fit of score on log(params) with residuals (Table 6, Fig. 7), bear on V6 in a new setting. The authors assume scores should be log-linear in size and blame departures on benchmark difficulty polarization, not on scaling itself. I chose T3 over T5 because they do not argue V6 is wrong. There is no loss, token, compute or allocation measurement, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. The main contribution, STEM versus random and Bayesian evaluation, is the study's own method and not a scaling result.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue that difficulty polarization in benchmarks (excess easy and hard items) and contamination make scores depart from a log-linear scaling trend. They treat this as benchmark bias, not a failure of scaling. They propose STEM, built from Qwen3 items that flip once from wrong to right with scale. STEM placed LLaMA3-8B and GLM4-9B correctly in 100% of trials, against 100%/88% for random sampling and 0% for the Bayesian baseline. They also overstate the residual pattern as uniform: GPQA, MATH and SuperGPQA have negative mid-size residuals.
record.recipe_differences: This is an analysis of zero-shot benchmark accuracy across an existing model family, not a reproduction of pretraining-loss scaling-law experiments. It fits benchmark scores against log parameter count and analyzes residuals.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences among benchmarks and attributes curve shape and residual patterns to their sample difficulty distributions. Experiments use zero-shot, non-CoT prompting; no prompt-setting comparison is reported for the scaling analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-item correctness across the eight Qwen3 sizes is non-monotonic for a large share of items: 65.85% on GPQA, 53.20% SuperGPQA, 47.93% MMLU-Pro, 41.94% MATH, 37.72% MMLU, 13.16% GSM8K (Sec. 4.3, Fig. 2). The authors attribute this to contamination without testing it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Item-level downstream correctness is often non-monotonic in model scale, even where aggregate accuracy rises.

record.problems: The evidence concerns benchmark accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss, and the scaling fit uses eight model sizes from one family. The study attributes residual patterns to difficulty polarization but does not experimentally isolate that cause. It also reports non-monotonic scores on some benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the 12 external-model benchmark scores for LLaMA3-8B and GLM4-9B because they are used to assess relative capability with STEM rather than as a parameter-scale sweep. Omitted the aggregate score column in Appendix Table 8 because it combines benchmark scores. Omitted individual residual values in Appendix Table 6 and residual-distribution statistics in Table 7 to remain within the 60-row limit; the text's reported residual pattern is captured in R49-R54. Table 1 is cited technical-report data and was not counted as a study result.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits are extrapolated to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters and tokens.
No shape or architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated data, or fine-tuning/transfer regimes.

Performance against pretraining loss or compute is not tested. Size is the only axis: eight models of one family, with MoE models counted by total parameters (30B, 235B) rather than active (3B, 22B). No uncertainty is given for the scores. GSM8K and MATH are scored by an unspecified judge prompt.
No loss-law exponents, training setups, fitting methods or compute-optimal splits are compared.

missing.what: Share of items whose correctness is non-monotonic across Qwen3 sizes, per benchmark (13.16%–65.85%).

record.verdict_notes: R01–R48 compare each model only with the 0.6B model, which shows direction but not predictability. The trend across sizes and the residual rows carry the V6 evidence. Table 1 (technical-report scores) and the Table 2 discriminability values derived from it are cited data and correctly excluded. The record's 'uncertainty_reported: y' holds only for the random-sampling table (Table 9); the scaling scores and fits carry no uncertainty. Total-parameter counting for the MoE models affects the log(P) fit and residuals.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures benchmark accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
It does not fit small-run loss curves and predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget parameter/token allocation is evaluated.
It does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
It does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as scaling regimes.
Tests downstream benchmark accuracy against parameter scale, not performance against pretraining loss or a broader set of downstream tasks.

Tests benchmark-score fit shape and sample-difficulty effects. It does not compare fitted loss exponents, training setups, or compute-optimal splits, and does not establish that published loss-law disagreements arise from particular fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Qwen3 0.6B–235B, zero-shot non-CoT, on MMLU, MMLU-Pro, SuperGPQA and GSM8K
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises nearly monotonically with size. Only near-ties remain (14B vs 30B on MMLU and GSM8K), and the largest model is highest on each (R01–R07, R09–R15, R25–R31, R33–R39).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased nearly monotonically, with near-ties between 14B and 30B on MMLU and GSM8K and the largest model scoring highest on every benchmark.

relationships.reason: GPQA is flat to lower from 0.6B to 4B (R22, R23). MATH is non-monotonic: 8B (81.36) and 4B (80.64) beat 14B, 30B and 32B (R41–R47).
relationships.display_finding: GPQA was flat or lower from 0.6B to 4B, while MATH scores of 81.36 at 8B and 80.64 at 4B exceeded those at 14B, 30B and 32B.

relationships.condition: Linear fit of score on log(total parameters), all six benchmarks
relationships.reason: Residuals are systematically negative at both ends, up to -10.6 points (GSM8K at 0.6B). The authors read this as a sigmoidal rather than log-linear curve; the pattern is irregular on GPQA and MATH (R49–R54).
relationships.display_finding: Residuals were systematically negative at both size extremes, reaching −10.6 points for GSM8K at 0.6B, suggesting sigmoid-shaped relationships with irregular GPQA and MATH patterns.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Broad comparison of Qwen3 models across the six benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Scores are generally higher for larger models than for Qwen3-0.6B; see R01-R08, R09-R16, R17-R24, R25-R32, R33-R40, and R41-R48.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPQA and MATH scores across Qwen3 model sizes
reader_labels.reason: Scores are not consistently monotonic: GPQA at 0.6B exceeds the 1.7B and 4B results, while MATH at 8B, 4B, and 1.7B exceeds the 14B, 30B-A3B, and 32B results; see R17-R24 and R41-R48.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Linear fits of Qwen3 benchmark accuracy against log parameter count on the six listed benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The reported residuals have a negative-positive-negative pattern across model sizes, which the authors interpret as a systematic departure caused by benchmark difficulty polarization and an S-shaped curve; see R49-R54.
